nodes.rationale: Live page (post 82380) built from factoryGPT.html via build_fgpt.py; paints an ECG canvas from CSS custom properties, which forces a MutationObserver on data-theme.

nodes.rationale: Live page (post 82462) built from 01-icrm-hub.standalone.html via build.py into icrm-hub-elementor.html; measured with getComputedStyle at 1440/768/390px rather than read from source.

nodes.label: Vertical-Native CRM Positioning
nodes.source_location: h2 'Not a horizontal CRM with a manufacturing skin.'

nodes.label: Dual-Theme Accessibility Rules
nodes.rationale: Adds a skip-to-content link and a forced-colors:active fallback (border:1px solid ButtonText on interactive controls) on top of the shared focus-visible and reduced-motion rules.

nodes.label: Reveal & Keyframe Animation System
nodes.rationale: IntersectionObserver .reveal/.in-view with directional variants and a six-step stagger, plus named keyframes (eco-idle-float, eco-flow, eco-float, zig-dots-flow, tele-pulse, poFadeUp). Always wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

nodes.label: CSS Architecture Checklist
nodes.rationale: Pre-submission gate covering scoping, !important, one-line rules, even-px sizes, token placement, gradient section blends, no inter-section borders, reduced-motion and forced-colors, and no raw colour values outside the token block.

nodes.label: Hero Pattern with Ecosystem Visual
nodes.rationale: 1.05fr/.95fr two-column hero with a radial brand glow and an SVG ecosystem diagram animated by stroke-dasharray pulse lines; min-height 100vh explicitly not required so content can breathe.

nodes.label: nth-of-type Section Gradient Alternation
nodes.rationale: Odd/even sections carry opposite linear-gradient fades so one colour bleeds into the next with no border-top, border-bottom or box-shadow ever placed between sections; transition:background-color .35s ease keeps the theme toggle smooth.

nodes.label: FBB Accessibility Implementation
nodes.rationale: Concrete implementation of the brand accessibility standards: :focus-visible ring, aria-hidden sprite root, role=dialog/aria-modal with focus in-and-back, and every animation wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference with a static fallback.

nodes.label: Inline SVG Icon Sprite System
nodes.rationale: One hidden inline <svg> sprite of <symbol> defs, instances via <use href="#i-name">; no icon font and no external library, and colour always inherited through currentColor so the same symbol serves every context.

nodes.label: Per-Section --cust-blend-from Gradient
nodes.rationale: Each section sets --cust-blend-from to the previous section's background and paints a 120-160px ::before gradient, so blending is order-aware and token-driven instead of hard-coded pairs; the hero is excluded because it is the top of the page.

nodes.label: IntersectionObserver Stat Count-Up
nodes.rationale: data-count-to / data-suffix attributes drive a requestAnimationFrame tween over 1200ms triggered at 0.4 threshold; omitting data-count-to leaves the stat as static text so qualitative claims share the same component.

nodes.label: Accent Red #C00000
nodes.rationale: Restricted to secondary-CTA fill only and never used as a background, so red stays rare and high-impact rather than becoming a second brand surface.

nodes.label: Brand Accessibility Standards
nodes.rationale: Focus outline in Primary Blue, decorative graphics hidden from AT, proper dialog semantics with focus trap and Escape, reduced-motion fallbacks, and the solid-badge contrast rule are treated as brand standards, not optional polish.

nodes.label: ITHENA Brand Colour System
nodes.rationale: Palette is kept intentionally minimal (one brand blue, one accent red, a light/dark neutral system) so every vertical page reads as the same brand. Brand colours are fixed and never re-picked per industry; only neutral surfaces and text shift between modes.

nodes.label: Custom Hand-Drawn Line Iconography
nodes.rationale: No icon fonts or third-party icon libraries — custom-drawn 24×24 single-weight shapes keep the visual language distinct; icons inherit colour via currentColor so one shape serves blue, white and text contexts.

nodes.label: Floating Status Cards
nodes.rationale: Elevated cards overlapping the hero image with a pulsing green dot (#1EA672) signalling live data — the motif reinforces ITHENA's real-time, connected-factory positioning and should appear wherever live monitoring is communicated.

nodes.label: Solid Icon Badge Component
nodes.rationale: 48px circle, solid Primary Blue fill, white icon — always solid, never a pastel/tinted background, because a light blue tint fails accessible contrast for the icon on top. Stated as a firm brand + accessibility rule, not a stylistic option.

nodes.label: Primary Blue #0083C8
nodes.rationale: Single primary brand colour for buttons, icons, links, badges and stat cards; theme-independent so it carries identity across light and dark.

nodes.label: Seven-Section Page Rhythm
nodes.rationale: Hero → Stats → Challenges → Solution 1 → Solution 2 → Business Value → Video/CTA banner is held constant across verticals; only copy, icons, dashboard labels, stat figures and imagery change per industry.

nodes.label: Stats Bar KPI Strip
nodes.rationale: Solid brand-blue card with a three-column KPI strip; numbers count up on scroll to draw attention to proof points, or stay static for qualitative claims like 'Zero downtime'.

nodes.label: Even-Pixel Type Scale
nodes.rationale: All sizes are fixed even-pixel values (48/32/24/18/16/14/12) with no fractional or fluid type, so pages built by different hands land on identical rhythm.

nodes.label: Case Studies Branch
nodes.rationale: The only top-level branch with no children — a flat link rather than a mega-panel, which the dynamic header's tree-shape inference renders differently.

nodes.label: Company Branch
nodes.rationale: Flat leaf list (Who We Are, Blogs, Announcements, Partnerships, Careers) — renders as a flat-card mega-panel rather than a column/group layout.

nodes.label: Performance Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Appears twice in the tree — under After Market Services and under Manufacturer > Production — so the same offering is reached from two audience paths.

nodes.label: Services Branch
nodes.rationale: Advisory Consulting, Data Management, Cloud Modernization, Business Transformation, Manufacturing Integration — each a group with two leaf offerings.

nodes.label: Solutions Branch
nodes.rationale: Three audience columns — OEM|Distributors (Front Office Ops, After Market Services), Manufacturer (Planning, Production, Quality, Maintenance), Enterprise (Supply Chain, Data Analytics, Apps).

nodes.label: Packaging Page Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Heading hierarchy, contrast, keyboard navigation, visible focus, accessible video controls, alt text, semantic HTML and reduced-motion support requested up-front in the brief rather than retrofitted.

nodes.label: Packaging Business Value Section
nodes.rationale: Five outcomes — increase aftermarket revenue, reduce service costs, improve customer experience, increase machine availability, create connected equipment — framing installed equipment as a continuous digital revenue channel.

nodes.label: Packaging Challenges Section
nodes.rationale: Unplanned downtime, complex spare parts, multi-SKU changeovers, lost aftermarket revenue, fragmented customer experience — followed by a visual transition from traditional to intelligent, self-servicing equipment.

nodes.label: Intelligent Packaging Ecosystem Flow
nodes.rationale: Machine → Telemetry → AI Insights → Predictive Maintenance → Spare Parts Identification → Digital Commerce → Order → Service → Customer, drawn with animated data-flow connections to communicate that ITHENA links the physical machine to digital commerce and service operations.

nodes.label: iSERV AI-Powered Spare Parts Commerce
nodes.rationale: Interactive visual cataloguing plus AI image-to-part recognition and automated order routing; presented as a workflow (part image → AI recognition → correct part → catalogue → cart → order → routing) rather than a feature list, to make the revenue mechanism legible.

nodes.label: Machine Telemetry & IIoT Analytics
nodes.rationale: Real-time throughput, OEE and wear-and-tear forecasting for packaging equipment; the analytics interface must be visually connected back to the physical machine so telemetry reads as attached to an asset, not abstract.

nodes.label: Tangible Outcomes Stats
nodes.rationale: Up to 40% aftermarket revenue increase, 50% faster order processing, 30% reduction in field unplanned downtime — each paired with its causal mechanism so the section communicates measurable business outcomes rather than displaying bare statistics.

nodes.label: ITHENA Site Navigation Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Five top-level branches (Solutions, Services, Industries, Case Studies, Company). Solutions is segmented by audience (OEM|Distributors, Manufacturer, Enterprise) rather than by product, so a visitor self-selects by role before meeting product names.

nodes.label: Packaging Landing Page Brief
nodes.rationale: Authoring prompt for the Packaging vertical. The stated objective is to sell business transformation and measurable outcomes, not a list of software features, and to feel like a premium enterprise platform built specifically for packaging machinery.

nodes.label: Even-Pixel Font Size Rule
nodes.rationale: All font sizes must be even integers in px, including clamp() endpoints; any value resolving odd rounds up to the next even integer. Enforced as a checklist item so pages built at different times stay on one scale.

nodes.label: main.[page-slug] Scoping & Isolation
nodes.rationale: Same isolation goal as the FBB spec but keyed to a slug class root (main.packaging-landing) rather than an id. Every property marked !important to prevent theme bleed; one declaration per line; non-colour rules inherited once from the root and never duplicated inside theme overrides.

nodes.label: Solid Badge Contrast Fix
nodes.rationale: A 15% brand tint behind the badge icon measured ~1.1:1 contrast; switching to solid brand fill with a white icon fixed it. Recorded as project history from tool-die-landing.html so the tinted variant is never reintroduced.

nodes.label: New Industry Page Extension Rules
nodes.rationale: Explicit constant-vs-variable split: colour tokens, type stack, section rhythm, radii, badge treatment and blend rhythm are fixed; copy, icon selection, dashboard values, stat figures and imagery vary. Icons must be semantically appropriate to the vertical rather than reused verbatim (don't carry bakery oven/flame icons onto packaging or defense).

nodes.label: Motion & Interaction Principles
nodes.rationale: Motion is subtle and purposeful — it reinforces credibility and a 'live system' feel, never decorative flourish. Scroll reveal, stat count-up, live-status pulse and remembered theme preference are the sanctioned moments, and every animated element must have a reduced-motion static fallback.

nodes.label: Alternating Sections with Soft Blend
nodes.rationale: Surface A/B alternate down the page with a gradient blend at the top of each section and never a hard dividing line, so the page reads as one continuous surface instead of stacked blocks with visible seams.

nodes.label: Formidable Label Contrast Defect
nodes.rationale: Formidable's default 11px #8D959F labels measured 3.03:1 on the white panel, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum; overriding to 12px/700 in --muted/--ink-3 raised it to 5.74:1 light and 5.89:1 dark.

nodes.label: Packaging Page Design Constraints
nodes.rationale: Explicit negative constraints: avoid generic corporate design, excessive gradients, excessive glassmorphism, neon AI styling and unnecessary animation. Positive constraints restate the brand system — #0083c8 primary, light #FFFFFF/#D7ECF6 and dark #123049/#0D1B2E section backgrounds, smoothly blended section intersections with no hard border, even-px font sizes, professional SVG icons instead of emojis.

nodes.label: #main-section data-theme Contract
nodes.rationale: Every landing page scopes its whole light/dark palette to a data-theme attribute on its own section#main-section wrapper (not <html>), because the page is injected into an existing WordPress/Astra document whose root element the page does not own. The header plugin independently sets data-theme on the same #main-section, making that attribute the de-facto integration contract between the site header and any page body. Divergence risk: the pages persist their choice under localStorage key 'fbb-theme' while wp-header-shortcode.php persists under 'ithena-theme', so header and page can disagree after reload.

nodes.label: Pre-Paint Theme Init (FOUC prevention)
nodes.rationale: Theme resolution is hooked to wp_head at priority 1 rather than living inside the shortcode output, so it runs in <head> before first paint no matter where on the page the header shortcode is placed - preventing a light-to-dark flash. It reads localStorage key 'ithena-theme' inside try/catch (private browsing throws), falls back to prefers-color-scheme, and mirrors the resolved value onto #main-section's data-theme so page-level dark/light CSS follows the header toggle.

nodes.label: Theme Storage Key Divergence (ithena-theme vs fbb-theme)
nodes.norm_label: theme storage key divergence (ithena-theme vs fbb-theme)
nodes.rationale: The header plugin persists theme under localStorage key 'ithena-theme' and renders its toggle as #theme-toggle, while every landing page persists under 'fbb-theme' and looks up #themeToggle. Both write data-theme onto the same #main-section element, so they agree within a session but can disagree after reload, and each side's toggle-binding lookup misses the other's element id. The pages compensate with a MutationObserver plus an idempotent bindToggle() that adopts whichever toggle element appears, but the two storage keys are never reconciled. Flagged as a latent integration bug rather than a deliberate design.

nodes.label: --m-std / --m-ease Motion Tokens
nodes.rationale: Two CSS custom properties carry the entire motion vocabulary: --m-std for the standard duration and --m-ease for the shared easing curve. Every transition on every page references these instead of literal values, so the whole design system's motion feel is retuned from one declaration block. The b2b page alone references them ~76 times.

nodes.label: .rv / .stg Scroll-Reveal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Shared reveal mechanism across all landing pages: elements tagged .rv are observed by an IntersectionObserver (threshold .16, rootMargin 0 0 -40px 0) that adds .on once and unobserves, so reveals never replay. .stg staggers children via per-index transition-delay. Any [data-count] descendant inside a revealed block animates a cubic ease-out counter over 1100ms. A second observer (threshold .55) toggles .on on .stop elements for scroll-pinned narrative beats. Critically the whole block is gated on prefers-reduced-motion: when reduced, every .rv and .stop is given .on immediately so content is never hidden from users who disabled motion - the reveal is progressive enhancement, not a display dependency.

nodes.label: Schedule-Demo Modal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every landing page ships an inert #schedulePopup shell with an empty #schedulePopupFormSlot, opened by any [data-schedule-demo] trigger. Rather than embedding a form per page, adoptScheduleForm() hunts the live DOM for a Formidable form (#schedule-demo-form, .schedule-demo-form, an Elementor .elementor-widget-shortcode containing .frm_forms, or a bare .frm_forms) and physically relocates that node into the slot, guarded by a scheduleFormMoved latch. This keeps the static HTML prototype identical to the WordPress-deployed page: the marketing team drops a Formidable widget anywhere on the page and it is silently teleported into the modal, so the prototype never has to hardcode form markup that WP would duplicate. Adoption is attempted on DOMContentLoaded, on window load, and again on modal open to survive late-rendering Elementor widgets.

nodes.label: Header DOM Relocation to body
nodes.rationale: JS moves the header, mobile panel and overlay to be direct children of <body> at runtime. Elementor wraps the shortcode in animated section containers whose transform/filter properties create a containing block that breaks position:fixed and traps z-index, so the header would scroll away or render under page content. Relocating makes the header immune to wherever on the page the shortcode was dropped. Consequence: depth-based font-weight CSS is scoped to :root rather than the header element, since the relocated nodes become siblings.

nodes.label: menu_subtitle ACF Field (with WP description fallback)
nodes.norm_label: menu_subtitle acf field (with wp description fallback)
nodes.rationale: Column and item subtitles come from an ACF field menu_subtitle read per menu item, assigned over $item->description. The function_exists('get_field') guard plus the overwrite-only-if-truthy check means the header degrades to the native WP menu-item Description field when ACF is deactivated or the field is blank, so the plugin never hard-depends on ACF. A sibling menu_icon field falls back to a hardcoded remote cube-1.svg.

nodes.label: Menu Tree Builder (shape-inferred mega-menu)
nodes.rationale: The header builds a two-pass tree from wp_get_nav_menu_items() on the WP menu 'new-ithena-menu': first pass indexes every item by ID into $refs and attaches an empty children array, second pass attaches each item to its menu_item_parent. Panel layout is then inferred from tree shape - a top-level item whose children themselves have children renders as a column/group mega-panel, a top-level item with only leaf children renders as flat cards. Nothing is hardcoded, so marketing can restructure the mega-menu entirely from Appearance > Menus without touching PHP.

nodes.label: adoptFbbForm()
nodes.rationale: Same relocate-by-CSS-ID mechanism as adoptScheduleForm but targeting #fbb-demo-form, hiding the hardcoded fallback form once adoption succeeds.

nodes.label: adoptScheduleForm()
nodes.rationale: Relocates (appendChild, never clones) a live Elementor Shortcode widget rendering [formidable id=...] into #schedulePopupFormSlot, so Formidable's own scripts, nonces and AJAX submit handler keep working untouched. Runs on DOMContentLoaded, window.load (late-rendering widgets) and every popup open; a scheduleFormMoved flag makes it idempotent.

nodes.label: adoptDemoForm()
nodes.rationale: Production instance of the form-adoption pattern on both live pages — runs on DOMContentLoaded, on load, and on every popup open, relocating the Formidable Shortcode widget into the modal.

nodes.label: Dual-Theme Colour Token Set
nodes.rationale: Richer token set than the FBB spec — adds brand gradients, glass tints, glow and a three-step shadow scale, and re-picks brand blue per theme (#0082c8 light → #2ea6e6 dark) so the accent stays legible on a navy ground.

nodes.label: Eight-Section Page Sequence
nodes.rationale: Extends the brand's seven-section rhythm with a final full-width gradient CTA banner + demo request form, and reorders Stats after Challenges.

nodes.label: Dual-Theme Token Architecture
nodes.rationale: Light is always the default with no attribute; dark is main.page-slug[data-theme="dark"]. A bare [data-theme] selector without the page-slug parent is forbidden because it would escape the isolation boundary and hit the host theme.

nodes.label: Fixed Theme Toggle Button
nodes.rationale: Sun/moon swap done purely with scoped display rules under the data-theme attribute rather than JS icon replacement, keeping the toggle stateless in script.

nodes.label: Request a Demo Modal ([data-demo-cta])
nodes.rationale: One shared overlay wired to every [data-demo-cta] trigger, shipping a hardcoded fallback form so the popup works before an Elementor form is wired up. Escape closes via a permanent document listener.

nodes.label: New Industry Page Checklist (FBB)
nodes.rationale: Verification gate before shipping a new vertical page — copy the token blocks verbatim because brand colours are shared across all ITHENA pages and must not be reinvented.

nodes.label: Schedule Discovery Call Modal ([data-schedule-demo])
nodes.rationale: Empty-slot variant that shows nothing until a live Formidable widget is adopted; stricter lifecycle than §7.8 — Escape listener attached/detached per open-cycle rather than left permanently on document, body scroll locked, focus sent to the first field and returned to the trigger. Pick one trigger attribute per page; never mix the two modal patterns.

nodes.label: FBB Seven-Section Sequence
nodes.rationale: Reusable skeleton — keep section order, swap eyebrow/heading copy, icon choices, dashboard tile labels/values and stat numbers. The footer is deliberately left out of the widget and inherited from the host theme.

nodes.label: data-theme Attribute Theme Architecture
nodes.rationale: Themes swap via a data-theme attribute on the root section rather than swapping stylesheets or classes; only colour tokens are overridden in the dark block while spacing/radius/grid/transition tokens are declared once, so the override surface stays small. Persisted via localStorage 'cust-theme'.

nodes.label: Assertion-Checked Build Scripts (build.py / build_fgpt.py)
nodes.rationale: Pages are generated from a source file by an assertion-checked script then uploaded verbatim so local and live match byte-for-byte. build_fgpt.py asserts no h3-matching selector declares above 32px; build.py re-encodes 8 inline PNG screenshots to WebP at 1600px/q78, cutting 3.09MB → 0.73MB and the page from 3.39MB → 1.03MB.

nodes.label: Elementor HTML + Shortcode Widget Architecture
nodes.rationale: One HTML widget (style + #main-section + script) plus one Shortcode widget rendering [formidable id=119], hidden in page flow and relocated into the modal. Elementor's hidden-desktop/tablet/mobile flags must NOT be used to hide it — they are display:none!important and survive the move, leaving the modal empty (food-beverage-bakery likely carries that bug).

nodes.label: Formidable Form ID 119
nodes.rationale: A single 'New - contact us form' serves both live pages and is adopted into each page's modal, so lead capture stays centralised rather than duplicated per page.

nodes.label: --header-h Published Variable
nodes.rationale: Header publishes its live height on <html> (116px → 100px on scroll); pages consume it via calc(). When no fixed header exists the page measures one and falls back to 0, never the 100px design-time default, which would reserve dead space.

nodes.label: window.ithenaTheme (header owns the theme)
nodes.rationale: The site header (wp-header-shortcode.php) is the single owner of theme state: it writes html.dark, persists localStorage['ithena-theme'] and mirrors data-theme onto #main-section. Page scripts must defer to it because both pages previously kept their own keys (ithena-microsite-theme, fgpt-theme) and raced the header.

nodes.label: Food & Beverage | Bakery Industry Page
nodes.rationale: The originating vertical — the whole ITHENA landing-page design system was distilled from this page's implementation.

nodes.label: [hidden] Broken by Scoped Reset
nodes.rationale: `section#main-section * { all:revert; }` strips the browser's default [hidden]{display:none} UA rule out of the cascade, so any element toggled via .hidden = true needs an explicit [hidden]{display:none!important} override. A direct side effect of the isolation strategy.

nodes.label: 999999 Modal Stacking Convention
nodes.rationale: The host sticky header (#site-header) runs z-index 999995, so any overlay must clear it or render behind. 999999 was chosen because it is the value already used site-wide in wp-header-shortcode.php's .demo-overlay/.mobile-panel/.scrim, rather than inventing an arbitrary new number.

nodes.label: Widget Scoping & Isolation (section#main-section)
nodes.rationale: The whole page is one Elementor HTML widget scoped to a single id root with `all:revert` and `!important` on every property, so the host Astra theme cannot leak in and the page cannot leak out. One rule per line keeps the block scannable and diff-friendly.

nodes.label: Dual Light/Dark Mode Brand Rule
nodes.rationale: Every page must ship both a light and dark presentation toggled by the viewer, never hard-coded to one mode; brand blue and accent red hold their value across modes so only the neutral system swaps.

nodes.label: Accents Re-picked Per Theme
nodes.rationale: Accent colours are re-picked rather than reused across themes — the dark mint #3FE0A0 would fail contrast on a light ground, so light mode uses #0A7A52. Contrast audit found 0 headings below 3:1 across both pages and themes.

nodes.label: ithena-bridge REST API Limits
nodes.rationale: POST /wp-json/ithena-bridge/v1/posts/{id}/elementor is flaky above ~800KB and fails intermittently at 1MB, so retry loops are required; /el/*, /site and /measurement/forms are blocked outright, likely by a WAF.

nodes.label: Chat Bubble z-index Blocking Submit
nodes.rationale: The site chat widget sits at z-index 2147483647 (max int) and swallowed taps on the modal Submit button, making the form unsubmittable on mobile. No z-index can beat max-int, so the fix hides #chatBubbleRoot for the duration the modal is open via body:has(...is-open).

nodes.label: Container Queries for Column Components
nodes.rationale: Viewport width stopped being a component's width the moment it moved into an Elementor column, so the iCRM hero mock keys its 208px sidebar to @container (max-width:760px) on .hero-shot instead of a media query.

nodes.label: Headings Must Declare color: inherit
nodes.rationale: The host theme sets an explicit colour on h1-h6 and an explicit colour beats an inherited one at any specificity, so var(--text) never reaches headings in dark mode. `inherit` also lets headings inside deliberately dark blocks (.cta-card, .tcard.dark) keep their own light colour.

nodes.label: reCAPTCHA Mobile Clipping Defect
nodes.rationale: The widget draws at a fixed 304px but its wrappers were forced to the 284px container with overflow:hidden, cutting the badge and privacy links; Formidable's own scale(0.86) then shrank an already-clipped box. Fix restores the natural 304px width so the existing scale fits the whole widget.

nodes.label: Scoped Reset & Host Plugin Gotchas
nodes.rationale: Catalogue of side effects of living inside a hostile host page: [hidden] stripped by the scoped reset; svg{max-width:100%} collapsing icons to 0 width inside a grid place-items:center parent; a popup/consent plugin leaving body{overflow:auto} inline which turns body into a scroll container and silently kills every position:sticky; and declaration order beating intuition, requiring section#main-section (0,1,2) over #main-section (0,1,1).

nodes.label: Industrial IoT & Predictive Maintenance Platform
nodes.rationale: ML models claimed to be purpose-built for compressor thermal and vibration patterns; thermal pattern analysis, vibration monitoring, predictive failure alerts, multi-unit fleet benchmarking.

nodes.label: Remote Diagnostic & Service Management (iSERV)
nodes.rationale: Automated ticket creation from compressor telemetry, remote parameter tuning, dynamic technician dispatch - explicitly sold on cutting truck rolls and improving first-time-fix rate.

nodes.label: Grid IoT & Substation Asset Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Real-time transformer & load sensing, secure validated data ingestion, predictive failure alerts, full asset traceability across transformers, substations and feeder lines.

nodes.label: iSERV Validated Performance & Ticketing System (Grid)
nodes.rationale: 'Every Fault Becomes a Tracked Work Order' - automated fault & outage ticketing, preventive maintenance logging, safety inspection workflow enforcement, real-time crew dispatch alerts.

nodes.label: Enterprise Business Intelligence & AI Platform
nodes.rationale: Underwriting risk evaluation scoring, customer propensity scoring, automated financial reporting, predictive churn & cancellation alerts - explicitly layered on top of the iRDS unified data lake.

nodes.label: iRDS Big Data & Customer Intelligence Engine
nodes.norm_label: irds big data & customer intelligence engine
nodes.rationale: Policy record integration across every line of business, claims history unification, live interaction touchpoint tracking - producing 'a single governed customer record - the foundation every cross-sell model and risk score depends on'.

nodes.label: Single Governed Customer Record
nodes.rationale: The recurring architectural claim on the data-platform pages: predictive scoring is only credible once every source system feeds one governed record, so unification is sold as a prerequisite rather than a feature.

nodes.label: CMS Modernization & Accessibility Engine
nodes.rationale: Solution block 1: WCAG 2.1/Section 508 auditing, ARIA-compliant components, one maintainable CMS framework replacing a dozen legacy portals, responsive design. Positioned as 'accessible by default' so compliance is not a retrofit.

nodes.label: iRDS Data Platform (product family)
nodes.rationale: Named ITHENA data platform re-skinned per industry: 'iRDS Public Sector Data Transparency Platform' (government), 'iRDS Big Data & Customer Intelligence Engine' (fintech/insurtech), 'iRDS Unified Retail Data Platform' (retail/CPG). Constant pitch across all three: aggregate siloed source systems into one governed source of truth that downstream analytics depend on.

nodes.label: iRDS Public Sector Data Transparency Platform
nodes.norm_label: irds public sector data transparency platform
nodes.rationale: Solution block 2: high-security data governance pipelines, open-data publishing, interactive public reporting dashboards, multi-department interoperability. Sold on standing up to public records requests and oversight.

nodes.label: IntersectionObserver Reveal-on-Scroll
nodes.rationale: .reveal elements get .in-view at threshold 0.15 and are then unobserved; under prefers-reduced-motion or no IntersectionObserver every .reveal is marked in-view immediately so content is never hidden.

nodes.label: Inline SVG Icon Sprite
nodes.rationale: A display:none aria-hidden <svg><defs> block of <symbol> ids (i-eye, i-shield, i-check, i-clock, i-play, i-close, i-sun, i-moon, plus industry-specific ones like i-accessibility, i-thermo, i-ticket) referenced via <use href='#i-...'/>. Kept inline so the page has zero external icon-font/CDN dependency when pasted into WordPress.

nodes.label: iSERV Service & Ticketing Platform (product family)
nodes.rationale: Named ITHENA service platform re-skinned per industry: 'iSERV Validated Performance & Ticketing System' (pharma, energy) and 'Remote Diagnostic & Service Management (iSERV)' (compressed air). Constant pitch: telemetry/deviation automatically becomes a tracked, audit-logged work order routed to the right crew.

nodes.label: iSERV Validated Performance & Ticketing System (Pharma)
nodes.rationale: Audit-ready incident tracking, preventive maintenance logging, SOP workflow enforcement, automated deviation routing to quality and maintenance teams.

nodes.label: Pharma IoT & Cleanroom Environmental Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Real-time temperature & pressure sensing, secure validated data ingestion, predictive drift alerts, full batch traceability - catching temperature/pressure/mixing drift before a batch is compromised.

nodes.label: iRDS Unified Retail Data Platform
nodes.rationale: POS integration across stores and regions, warehouse/inventory synchronization, real-time e-commerce order unification - producing 'a single governed SKU and customer view' that forecasting and replenishment depend on.

nodes.label: Predictive Demand & Merchandising Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Store-level demand forecasting, dynamic pricing & promotion analytics, predictive stockout/overstock alerts, automated replenishment recommendations.

nodes.label: Compressed Air OEM Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Guarantee Uptime for Connected Compressed Air Systems', aimed at compressed air OEMs with an installed base of compressors, dryers and filtration systems. Pain points: undetected air leaks, unplanned pressure drops, thermal degradation & wear. Claimed outcomes: 25% lower warranty & service cost, 20% energy efficiency gain, 98% on-time servicing compliance.

nodes.label: Energy & Utility Operations Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Guarantee Grid Reliability and NERC CIP Compliance'. Pain points: NERC CIP & safety compliance, aging infrastructure under rising load, undetected equipment faults cascading into service-area outages. Claimed outcomes: 99.98% grid uptime, 45% faster outage response, 25% fewer unplanned asset failures.

nodes.label: Original .feature-visual Dashboard Mockup Markup
nodes.rationale: Backup of the hand-built HTML dashboard mockups (.dash-head / .dash-grid / .dash-tile with status tags) that previously filled every 'div.feature-visual reveal' slot, captured from the live dev-website pages before those slots were replaced with static screenshots. Header records the restore procedure: paste a block back in place of the . Covers 8 live pages: /compressed-air/ (Equipment Health, Service Ticket #7204), /custom-tool-builders/ (Build Workflow, Die Set DS-4471), /industrial/ (Data Ingestion, Work Order #2214, Asset Health), /discrete-automotive/ (Line Monitoring, Service Ticket #3312), /pharmaceutical/ (Batch Compliance Log, Cleanroom Zone A), /energy-utilities/ (Grid Compliance Log, Substation 4 Feeder Bank), /fintech-insurance/ (Customer Intelligence Profile, Risk & Underwriting Dashboard), /government/ (Accessibility Audit, Public Data Portal). No retail/CPG block, indicating that page postdates the capture.

nodes.label: FinTech & InsurTech Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Turn Siloed Policy, Claims, and Customer Data Into Predictive Intelligence'. Pain points: siloed customer & policy data, delayed claims processing, elevated policyholder churn. Claimed outcomes: 25% cross-sell/upsell lift, 70% faster claims reporting & BI, 30% churn reduction. Diverges from the manufacturing pages by replacing the 'Business Value' section with a 'Cost of Waiting' loss-framing recap and by swapping the demo CTA for 'Request a Data Architecture Review'.

nodes.label: Government & Public Sector Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Modernize Public Portals. Earn Public Trust.' Sector = government/public sector digital modernization. Pain points: accessibility mandates (WCAG 2.1 / Section 508 / ARIA), fragmented public portals, auditable data requirements. Claimed outcomes: 100% WCAG 2.1 & ARIA compliance, 3x faster multi-department reporting, 40% lower portal maintenance cost.

nodes.label: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Guarantee Compliance and Uptime for Pharmaceutical Manufacturing'. Pain points: GxP/FDA compliance, batch consistency under tight process tolerances, deviation traceability. Claimed outcomes: 100% regulatory compliance & batch traceability, 60% faster incident resolution, 30% lower batch scrap. Source comments flag that the Hero and Business Value sections were NOT in the supplied content spec - they were drafted to fit the compliance/uptime theme (Business Value deliberately only restates the three stats, 'no new claims introduced') and are marked 'Review before publishing'.

nodes.label: Retail & CPG Landing Page
nodes.rationale: Pitch: 'Unify POS, Inventory & E-Commerce Data for Real-Time Insights'. Pain points: siloed POS/inventory/e-commerce data, reactive stockouts and overstock, missed promotion & pricing windows. Claimed outcomes: 35% fewer stockout-driven lost sales, 3x faster forecast cycles, 20% lower inventory carrying cost. Structurally the closest sibling of the FinTech page - same 'Cost of Waiting' recap and 'Request a Data Architecture Review' CTA.

nodes.label: Viewport-Triggered Animated Stat Counter
nodes.rationale: data-count-to / data-suffix attributes drive a 1200ms requestAnimationFrame ramp fired by an IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.4 on #s-stats. Honors prefers-reduced-motion by jumping straight to the final value, and falls back to instant render when IntersectionObserver is absent.

nodes.label: Elementor/Formidable Demo Form Adoption Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every page ships a hardcoded fallback demo form, then on DOMContentLoaded/load/popup-open looks for a real form (#<prefix>-demo-form, .<prefix>-demo-form, any .elementor-widget-shortcode containing .frm_forms/form, or bare .frm_forms) and appendChild's the LIVE DOM node into the popup slot, hiding the fallback. Deliberately relocates rather than clones or re-renders so Formidable's own scripts, nonces and AJAX handlers keep working. Source comment documents the CSS-ID contract for the WP editor.

nodes.label: Section-Scoped Dark/Light Theme Toggle
nodes.rationale: data-theme is set on the page's own root <section class='<prefix>-landing'>, not on <html>, and persisted under a per-page localStorage key ('gov-theme', 'phm-theme', 'ca-theme', 'enu-theme', 'fti-theme', 'rcp-theme'). Scoping to the section lets the block be dropped inside a WordPress/Elementor page without fighting the site theme; the per-page key means the six pages do not share a theme preference. Default is 'dark'. localStorage access is try/catch-wrapped for private-browsing failures.

nodes.label: Shared Industry Landing Page Skeleton
nodes.rationale: One template instantiated per industry with a 3-letter prefix (gov/phm/ca/enu/fti/rcp) on every class, id and localStorage key. Fixed section order: inline SVG icon sprite -> Hero (eyebrow, h1, 3-item checklist, two CTAs, photo + floating status cards) -> Stats bar (3 animated counters) -> Intro/Challenges (3 icon columns) -> Feature block 1 (dash right) -> Feature block 2 (dash left, reversed) -> Business Value / 'Cost of Waiting' (3 icon columns) -> Video/CTA banner -> Request a Demo popup. Prefixing rather than sharing one stylesheet keeps each page a self-contained paste-into-Elementor unit, at the cost of duplicated CSS/JS across six files.
